The code an ndt_group() column is keyed on

Source: R/ndt-seam.R
ndt_bound_key.Rd

The addition-term registry coerces every ndt_group() column to a numeric code before any family sees it, because an addition term's value is baked into the tape as data. This is that coercion, exported so that a caller holding a raw grouping can build the aterms list ndt_bound() reads without going through frmtmb::frm().

Usage

ndt_bound_key(x)

Arguments

x

A grouping: a factor, character, logical or numeric vector.

Value

A numeric vector of codes, one per element of x.

Details

The code is a function of the group's LABEL and of nothing else, so a factor, a character vector, a logical and integer codes that name the same groups all give the same bound, and none of them depends on the level order of the frame the column was evaluated in.

It is a hash, and it is not injective

The code is two polynomial rolling hashes over the label's code points, packed into one double below 2^49. Two different labels CAN therefore share a code. Where both are in one column this refuses by name rather than merging them. Where they are not, that is, where a label the fit never saw collides with one it did, the unseen row is paired with the collided group's bound instead of being refused, at a rate of about 1.8e-15 per pairing.

That residual is structurally zero for the identifier shapes anyone uses: labels of one to three printable ASCII characters cannot collide at all, and all 10^8 identifiers of the form S00000000 hash to 10^8 distinct codes where a birthday count predicts 8.88 collisions. Constructing an actual collision needed labels differing in four positions over a span of 6401 code points.

See also

ndt_bound(), which reads the codes under the name ndt_group.

Examples

ndt_bound_key(factor(c("s1", "s2", "s1")))
#> [1] 253570877197 253587654414 253570877197
